sagacity

/suh-GAS-ih-tee/ - the stress falls on GAS · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Sagacity means wise, sound judgment.

Her sagacity showed less in what the garden club planted than in what she talked them out of planting.

Example

Two job offers, one obvious: the flashy startup paid a third more. Grandpa asked a single question - 'Which boss answered your emails during the interview month?' - and Nia took the smaller offer. Three years later the startup was gone and her patient employer had tripled her role. The family started calling Grandpa's question what it was: sagacity.

Sagacity is wisdom applied at decision time - judgment keen about people, patient about consequences, and usually proven right only later. Cleverness solves the puzzle in front of you; sagacity knows which puzzles are worth solving.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

wisdom: Wisdom is deep understanding of life and what matters, and it can sit quietly for years without ever being used. Sagacity is wisdom at work: sound judgment applied to a live decision — which offer, which risk — and usually proven right only later.

judgment: Judgment is the general faculty of deciding, and the word is neutral: judgment can be hasty, poor, or excellent. Sagacity is a verdict on quality — judgment so keen about people and consequences that time proves it wise.

prudence: Prudence is careful judgment aimed at avoiding harm — it counts costs, keeps reserves, and declines the gamble. Sagacity can be bold: its long view sometimes takes the very risk prudence would refuse, because it sees the decade beyond the danger.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

folly: foolish misjudgment

shortsightedness: seeing only the immediate step

Where it sits · how far ahead the judgment sees

sense → shrewdness → sagacity

sense vs. sagacity: Sense keeps you from obvious mistakes; sagacity operates far above it, weighing people and years, not just the next step.

shrewdness vs. sagacity: Shrewdness is sharp about the deal in front of it, sometimes narrowly so; sagacity is larger - shrewdness plus patience plus the long view.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — sagac-: keen-scented, quick to perceive (Latin sagax)

Suffix — -ity: state of being

Put it together: Sagac- (Latin sagax, 'keen-scented, quick to perceive') + -ity (the state of being) = the state of being keen-scented. The Romans used sagax first of hunting dogs that could smell a faint trail; a sagacious mind noses out the wise course the same way. English keeps the adjective sagacious, so sagacity is the state of being sagacious - and note it is not related to sage, the wise elder, which grew from a different Latin root.

Use the root in a new word: presage: You met presage in Course 1: sailors watched the falling barometer, certain it presaged a storm.

Word Choice

formal / literary

Sagacity is high praise for judgment proven wise over time - the stuff of biographies and case studies. Its neighbor in this unit, perspicacity, praises the seeing; sagacity praises the deciding. A scout with perspicacity spots the storm first; a captain with sagacity has already routed around it.
